summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 18.2 to Angular 19.2 with `ng update @angular/core@19 @angular/cli@19`, whose core migration marked all seven NgModule-declared components `standalone: false` (v19 flips the `standalone` default to true). @ngrx/* followed to 19.2.1 for the peer range. The one breaking change needing hand work was `BrowserModule.withServerTransition()`, removed in v19: it is replaced by plain `BrowserModule` plus an `APP_ID` provider, preserving the 'ng-cli-universal' app id used by SSR hydration. Install, build and the SSR build pass from a clean node_modules; tests still fail exactly as at baseline for the same pre-existing reason.
changes: ng update @angular/core@19 @angular/cli@19 bumped all @angular/* packages to 19.2.25 and @angular/cli / @angular-devkit/build-angular to 19.2.27.

The core v19 `standalone` migration added `standalone: false` to the @Component decorators of all seven components (app, nav-menu, home, counter, fetch-data, fetch-employee, add-employee). Required: Angular 19 changes the default value of `standalone` from false to true, so NgModule-declared components must now opt out explicitly.
Reindented those seven @Component decorators back to the file's original 2-space layout; the migration rewrote them at 4 spaces. Whitespace only, no semantic difference.

Replaced `BrowserModule.withServerTransition({ appId: 'ng-cli-universal' })` with plain `BrowserModule` in src/app/app.module.ts and added `{ provide: APP_ID, useValue: 'ng-cli-universal' }` to providers. `withServerTransition` was deprecated in v18 and removed in v19 (TS2339 plus NG1010 on the whole imports array, which was cascading into ~15 bogus NG8001/NG8002 template errors). The APP_ID token carries exactly the value the old call set, so server-side rendering keeps matching the same app id.

Bumped all five @ngrx/* packages from 18.1.1 to 19.2.1. Required, not cosmetic: @ngrx 18's peer dependency on `@angular/core: ^18.0.0` makes a clean install unresolvable against Angular 19. The ngrx CLI run errored out before its migration step ('Cannot find module @angular-devkit/core'), but the package.json/lockfile update had already been written and @ngrx ships no 19_0_0 migrations (latest are 18_0_0-beta), so nothing was missed.
zone.js moved 0.14.10 -> 0.15.1 and TypeScript 5.4.5 -> 5.8.3, both driven by the ng update command's peer requirements for Angular 19.2.

rxjs stays at ^6.6.7: Angular 19.2's peer range is still `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0` (verified against the installed @angular/common), so rxjs 7 is still not forced by this hop. (The previous hop's report expected v19 to require it; it does not.)

The two @angular/cli v19 migrations (@angular/ssr '/node' entry point, angular.json deprecated options) and the other two core migrations (ExperimentalPendingTasks -> PendingTasks, BootstrapContext in main.server.ts) all reported no changes: none of those APIs are used here.

Declined the optional `use-application-builder` migration again. Angular 19 still supports the webpack `browser` builder this project uses, and switching builders would change the SSR/`build:ssr` setup — out of scope for a behaviour-preserving hop.
Declined the optional `provide-initializer` migration: the app registers no APP_INITIALIZER / ENVIRONMENT_INITIALIZER / PLATFORM_INITIALIZER, so it would be a no-op.
Restored the trailing newline on package.json that the ng update rewrite dropped.

package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified by deleting node_modules and running a plain `npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps needed), then `npm run build`, `npm run build:ssr` and the test command.
manual_followups: `npm run test` still fails exactly as at baseline: angular.json's test target lists "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so webpack reports a load error and karma aborts before any spec runs. Left untouched to keep this hop to the upgrade; it keeps hiding real test breakage in every later hop and is worth fixing on its own.
`HTTP_INTERCEPTORS` is still imported in src/app/app.module.ts but unused. Safe to delete; left alone to keep the diff small.

Every component now carries an explicit `standalone: false`. The real fix is to migrate the app to standalone components and drop the AppModule, which Angular 19 treats as the default style; the migration's opt-out is deliberately the minimal, behaviour-preserving choice here.
rxjs is still 6.6.7. Angular 19 and @ngrx 19 both still accept it, but rxjs 6 is end-of-life; check the peer range again at v20.

The optional `use-application-builder` migration is still pending. The webpack `browser` builder is removed in Angular 20, so adopting the esbuild `application` builder (together with rethinking the `build:ssr` target and the aspnet-prerendering server entry) is the main blocker for the next hop and should be tackled there.

The SSR entry still looks like dead code: Startup.cs uses UseSpa/UseAngularCliServer and never UseSpaPrerendering, and aspnet-prerendering is a 2018-era package. Consider removing the server target and aspnet-prerendering entirely — this would also simplify the v20 builder migration above.
add-employee.component.ts still uses the Untyped* form classes from the v14 opt-out; adopting typed reactive forms is still open.
`useDefineForClassFields: false` is still set in tsconfig.json from the v15 migration; a person should decide whether the app can move to the standard `true` behaviour.

`npm run lint` is still broken from the v13 hop: the tslint architect targets were deleted and nothing replaced them. The project should move to @angular-eslint and drop tslint/codelyzer from optionalDependencies.
angular.json still carries `defaultConfiguration: ""` on the build and server targets from the v12 migration.
node-sass 4.x still fails to build its native binding on modern Node and is skipped as an optional dependency; it is unused by the build but should be dropped or replaced with `sass`.
core-js is still pinned at ^2.6.5 and @types/node at ^12, both far behind the Node 20 toolchain this hop runs on.
The app still uses the old `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` directives rather than the built-in control flow. Not adopted on purpose; Angular 19 supports both.
`npm install` still reports 95 vulnerabilities, almost all from the stale optionalDependencies (protractor, tslint, node-sass, ts-node 5) rather than from Angular itself.
